video_title: BIGGEST Early All-Star Selection Debates - What STARS May Be Left Off?

quotes.speaker: Ben Golliver
quotes.summary_phrase: Ben Golliver on the difficulty of selecting NBA All-Stars
quotes.excerpt: you're kind of choosing between like second options on good teams or you're picking leading options on bad teams
quotes.quote: There is a lot of chalk on this year's outlook. You have had a lot of stars on winning teams play very well, so that makes it less interesting. When you dig down a little bit deeper to the bottom of the roster though, especially in the East, that's where it gets tricky because you're kind of choosing between like second options on good teams, so like the Paul Georges and the Bam Adebayos of the world, or you're picking leading options on bad teams. So it might be Anthony Davis with Washington with his huge numbers, Franz Wagner with Wendell Carter Jr. and his huge numbers. Maybe they are not quite bad anymore, but they are still mediocre. So those were some of the debates that I was getting into.

quotes.speaker: Ben Golliver
quotes.summary_phrase: Debating Bam Adebayo versus Anthony Davis for All-Star selection
quotes.excerpt: Bam or AD? I think that was one of the toughest calls

text_blocks.speaker: Ben Golliver
text_blocks.text: I just throw this to you: Bam or AD? I think that was one of the toughest calls. Obviously, one's having a lot more success team-wise, one's got bigger numbers. Where are you guys coming down on that one?

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Both of them have had some huge games, but have kind of been up and down.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim Bontemps
text_blocks.text: Honestly, the thing I see on the East is there's a 22-time All-Star who I'm not finding his name on here. And I just got to tell you, there's not going to be an All-Star game without LeBron James having a spot on a roster.

quotes.speaker: Ben Golliver
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James's All-Star case based on early season impact
quotes.excerpt: I just didn't think he was one of the 12 best players in the East to this point
quotes.quote: I would note last year, he was actually voted in by the coaches. He was not voted in by the fans because remember he had the sciatica. He was injured. You look at his impact to start the season, I just didn't think he was one of the 12 best players in the East to this point. I don't think he would tell you—well, maybe I don't want to put it in his mouth—but I think he would admit that he has had better years. But their team is first in the East. They are going to get multiple All-Stars.

quotes.speaker: Ben Golliver
quotes.summary_phrase: Ben Golliver's 76ers power rankings and All-Star projections
quotes.excerpt: I had him third on my 76ers power rankings. I had Maxey one, then Brown, then LeBron
quotes.quote: I had him third on my 76ers power rankings. I had Maxey one, then Brown, then LeBron. I could easily see a situation where all three get in. Adam Silver has made some commissioner picks in the past. There's always injury replacements. I mean there's all these different ways you could make it.

quotes.speaker: Tim Bontemps
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim Bontemps on the distinction between All-Star and best player
quotes.excerpt: I think if you're saying who are the 12 best players in the Eastern Conference, I would leave him off
quotes.quote: I think if you're saying who are the 12 best players in the Eastern Conference, I would leave him off. I think if you're saying who are the All-Stars, you're not leaving him off.

quotes.speaker: Ben Golliver
quotes.summary_phrase: Ben Golliver's case for Anthony Davis as an All-Star
quotes.excerpt: I kind of made the conscious decision to not punish him for Trae Young's start
quotes.quote: Let me make the case for AD, and I'll admit it's a little bit of a half-hearted case because the Wizards are the Wizards at this point. But I kind of made the conscious decision to not punish him for Trae Young's start. If you look at the on-off numbers, the Wizards are a lot better when they've got Anthony Davis on the court than they are when they've got Trae Young on the court. He's averaging 25 and nine. There's only three guys in the NBA who are doing it. The other two guys are like MVP-level players. I think in terms of what I expected from Anthony Davis this season individually, he's done everything I would have guessed and more, and he's stayed healthy, which was the big problem in Dallas and at times in Los Angeles in his previous stops.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on LeBron James's role and defensive impact
quotes.excerpt: I've seen LeBron playing all kinds of different roles. I see him being a force multiplier
quotes.quote: I've seen LeBron playing all kinds of different roles. I see him being a force multiplier in the clutch. I see him being sort of an emotional leader of that team. I'm seeing a whole lot of stuff out of the whole Philly operation that makes you say honor these folks. But your point about the numbers is not wrong. The AD numbers are very good.

quotes.speaker: Tim Bontemps
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim Bontemps on the Western Conference All-Star logjam
quotes.excerpt: It looks like there's two teams in the West that have multiple selections
quotes.quote: It looks like there's two teams in the West that have multiple selections, and neither of them are the two teams that are tied at top the West standings. Jamal Murray is absolutely an All-Star. He is an All-Star. And then, you know, leaving Kevin Durant off is also an extremely dicey.

quotes.speaker: Ben Golliver
quotes.summary_phrase: Ben Golliver on team construction and All-Star selections
quotes.excerpt: It's also about team construction. You've got kind of a top-heavy team there in Denver
quotes.quote: It's also about team construction. You've got kind of a top-heavy team there in Denver where Jokic and Murray, you have to take both of those guys. There's no way to choose between them. They've both been lights out and they're picking up a little momentum here lately. Now when you look at Houston, it's trickier. It's an incredible trivia question right now: who's the leading scorer on the NBA's most efficient offense? The answer is Alperen Sengun. They're such a balanced attack there in Houston. All five starters in double figures, KD taking a smaller role. But again, you look at the on-off numbers, Houston starters have been very strong. Sengun's been great, KD's been great. That's why I went that direction. I think a guy like Reeves is somebody to highlight though. When healthy, he's absolutely deserved to be an All-Star. He's got the numbers, he's got the impact. Their offense when Luka and Reeves are both healthy has been off the charts.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on Stephen Curry's MVP status and injury
quotes.excerpt: Stephen Curry's MVP status has been burnished by the Warriors collapsing since he got injured
quotes.quote: Stephen Curry's MVP status has been burnished by the Warriors collapsing since he got injured. Well, it's like the record's almost exactly flipped: seven and three with him, four and seven without him. And they would have been three and eight if they didn't steal that one late against Boston the other night.

quotes.speaker: Ben Golliver
quotes.summary_phrase: Ben Golliver on Rudy Gobert's All-Star case
quotes.excerpt: You need at least one person from Minnesota. Rudy, the finishing stuff and the hands around the baskets
quotes.quote: I was curious actually what Tim would think here because it's been a number of years since Rudy made it. Obviously, you need at least one person from Minnesota. Rudy, the finishing stuff and the hands around the baskets, getting all this negative attention, but you look at their defense, number one in the league, better than San Antonio with Wembanyama, better than everybody else. Rudy's individual defensive rating completely off the charts. So you could make a case for him. I went with Luka not only for his scoring and playmaking, but just the vibes. Being able to bring guys together, Ayo's in a new role. You've got Cam coming in for a new team and it feels like he's been the star that's the straw that stirs the drink for Minnesota.

quotes.speaker: Tim Bontemps
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim Bontemps on Rudy Gobert's defensive impact
quotes.excerpt: They're not just number one in the league defensively, they're number one in the league by a comfortable margin
quotes.quote: They're not just number one in the league defensively, they're number one in the league by a comfortable margin, and Rudy is absolutely the anchor of all that. He's a four-time defensive player of the year who's playing as well on that end as he ever has. I get the Luka argument. Luka does not have All-Star individual numbers, like the scoring, doesn't have the assist, doesn't have the percentages. But if you watch them play, you know just how much he is essential to their offense. I could make an argument that their best player has been Luka.

quotes.speaker: Ben Golliver
quotes.summary_phrase: Ben Golliver on the hardest teams to divvy up All-Star credit
quotes.excerpt: The two teams I thought were the hardest to divvy up the credit was Minnesota
quotes.quote: The two teams I thought were the hardest to divvy up the credit was Minnesota because, as you mentioned, three candidates potentially, and Jaden McDaniels is no slouch either. And then you look at Atlanta where you've got Jaylen Johnson the returning All-Star. He's kind of not been off to a super hot start shooting the basketball but still very productive. You've got Nikola Alexander-Walker as their leading scorer. And then you've got kind of a hipster pick with Dyson Daniels where there's like a Dyson Daniels hive of Dyson Daniels fans online who are pointing to just off-the-charts impact numbers, incredible defense, kind of as a tone-setter for them. Now there aren't a lot of All-Stars in the past who fit that profile. It's a pretty rare deal, but again, it's like who's been the most important hawk? It's an interesting debate.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on Dyson Daniels's defensive impact
quotes.excerpt: Dyson Daniels had whoever he was guarding in hell. His arms are so long
quotes.quote: That game the other night where we mentioned it, he had Cade Cunningham and some of the other Pistons players in hell. The Hawks outscored the Pistons 33 to 12 in the fourth quarter. Dyson Daniels had whoever he was guarding in hell. His arms are so long and he make—he doesn't give you anything. He doesn't give you a free dribble, he doesn't give you a free dribble handoff, he doesn't give you a free like sideways pass. He's just—he's all up in you. He is—he is absolutely—like if you ever played him in a series, you would hate that guy. Hate him by the end of a playoff series.

quotes.speaker: Tim Bontemps
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim Bontemps on the value of defense in All-Star voting
quotes.excerpt: I just think you have to be—listen, offense is more valuable than defense. It just is
quotes.quote: I just think you have to be—listen, offense is more valuable than defense. It just is. It's reflected in the contracts, it's reflected in winning. And so, yes, I think the all-defensive team is enough for that. There are the rare players who are so dominant defensively, I think you can consider them as All-Stars, but he's still a pretty limited offensive player. But he does have a Hoop Collective tie-in, Wendy. He is an investor in Courtside Melbourne where we had our live show.

quotes.speaker: Ben Golliver
quotes.summary_phrase: Ben Golliver on his basketball roots and All-Star evolution
quotes.excerpt: I feel like I've kind of hit middle age on that though. When I was first making my All-Star picks
quotes.quote: Beaverton, Oregon born and raised, right? So you get the Nike in your bloodstream and on your feet pretty early. In terms of the hipster stuff, I feel like I've kind of hit middle age on that though. When I was first making my All-Star picks, maybe 10 years ago, a guy like Evan Mobley, right, or the Dyson Daniels, you know, he's underrated, he doesn't get enough attention. I would have been caping for those guys so hard. I would have definitely had Rudy probably as like the captain of my All-Star team this year just because, you know, you feel like they're not getting enough love and they have such a big impact on the game. But I kind of agree with what Tim said, offense has never been more important in the NBA. The numbers are just going crazy and so, if that's the way the game is being played, we're in this pace and space era, the All-Star game probably should reflect that.
